State lives in ~/Library/Application Support/Mucaro AI (mode 0700), outside the replaceable bundle. It is local by default and survives quit/relaunch and reinstall (macOS E2E). Runs are reconciled on restart.

Conversation runs support restart (RUNNING->INTERRUPTED), resume of waiting runs after restart, cancel/stop, partial-failure recovery via targeted retry, and idempotent resubmission. App-level restart of the packaged app is MATRIX-016.

Every capability classified AVAILABLE_LOCALLY / UNAVAILABLE_OFFLINE / REQUIRES_REMOTE_SERVICE (plus LOCAL_DEPENDENCY_MISSING); remote providers ineligible when offline. OPEN: UI offline states and network-interruption tests (MATRIX-016).
No frozen performance thresholds.

Structural guarantees: tool calls only from the user's own message, approvals only from user decisions or the documented auto policy, fenced sources with unforgeable closing tags, prompts never include credentials, grants only via explicit grant. Detection is advisory (documented false positives) and never gates or triggers actions.

Covers path traversal, absolute/backslash paths, bombs (ratio + actual bytes), symlink/executable/encrypted members, malformed/truncated archives, extension/content mismatch, executable payloads. Scope: ZIP-family archives (zip, docx); tar/7z/rar are UNSUPPORTED and never extracted.

Secrets are not committed (secret scan) or surfaced in evidence (evidence-field scan). The launch token stays out of receipts and logs, is kept in a 0600 instance file, and reaches the window only through the URL fragment. Prompts and exports never contain credentials. Residue: production API keys still come from environment variables; macOS Keychain storage is not implemented.

Permissions and their negative gates:
- Filesystem: directory grants.
- Network: remote tools need approval; SSRF/private-address blocking; the service listens on loopback only.
- Models: loopback-only local provider; routing modes local-only, remote-forbidden and offline.
- Tools: per-call approval bound to the argument digest; unknown tools are refused.
- External services: web search stays fail-closed without live permission and a key.
- Consequential actions: mutating tools need approval; a retry needs a fresh approval; untrusted content cannot create approvals.
- API: token boundary.
The security gate permission_boundaries checks the registry on every run.

Verification tooling exists; signing/notarization credentials unavailable (SIGNING_NOTARIZATION = BLOCKED).

Malformed, mislabeled, empty, truncated, encrypted, oversized, archive-attack and unsupported cases are covered; a declared format registry and a frozen benchmark receipt remain OPEN (TGT-012).

All nine action classes are covered with audit and state truthfulness: allowed, denied, approval-required, cancelled, tool error/crash (FAILED, never left RUNNING), TIMEOUT, retry (failed target only, fresh approval), restart (RUNNING -> INTERRUPTED, no auto-retry) and duplicate invocation (atomic claim, handler runs exactly once). TIMEOUT: every handler runs under a per-tool wall-clock bound (default 120 s). On expiry the call is FAILED with ERROR_TOOL_TIMEOUT (category TOOL_FAILURE) and handler_abandoned=true. A mutating tool is marked side_effects=UNKNOWN because Python cannot kill the thread. A late return is discarded and never recorded as EXECUTED. The audit log is hash-chained and tamper-evident.
Local-only, remote allowed, remote forbidden, unavailable local, unavailable remote, modality mismatch, context constraint and offline state; no case violates permissions.

All listed checks run in one gate (dependency scan, SBOM, secrets, static triage, permission, archive, prompt-injection, unsafe-path and network-boundary regressions, and packaging checks via the macOS build receipt). It runs in CI on every PR.

The builder freezes every MATRIX-020 entry. An entry that is unavailable is recorded explicitly as BLOCKED, NOT_APPLICABLE or MISSING, never omitted. Frozen at 0a806c1 with no missing entries (complete_except_blocked); signing and notarization are recorded as BLOCKED. A certified-release manifest cannot exist until signing (BLK-SIGN-001) and the remaining gates close.
